title: Conditional Rendering: v-if, v-else, v-show
description: Learn to show or hide elements based on conditions.

slides.title: Conditionally Render with v-if
slides.content:
# v-if, v-else-if, v-else These directives work exactly like JavaScript `if/else`: ```html

Excellent!

Good job!

Keep practicing!

``` Only one block is rendered at a time. If the condition is false, the element is **completely removed** from the DOM.

slides.title: v-show: Toggle Visibility
slides.content:
# v-show vs v-if `v-show` toggles the element's `display` CSS property, but it's always in the DOM. ```html

I'm still in the DOM, just hidden!

``` **When to use which?** - `v-if`: Expensive toggles (removes/creates elements) – better when condition rarely changes. - `v-show`: Frequent toggles – cheaper because element stays in DOM.

quizData.question: What is the main difference between `v-if` and `v-show`?

options.text: `v-if` removes the element from the DOM when false; `v-show` just hides it with `display: none`

quizData.explanation: `v-if` actually destroys/recreates the element, while `v-show` simply toggles visibility with CSS. Use `v-if` for rare toggles, `v-show` for frequent ones.
